problem:
The quadratic polynomial $P(x)$ has the double root ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-9.$ Find $P(x).$

$P(x)=$ {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-9,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})^{2} & =(-9){(x-3)}^{2} \\  & =-9(x-3)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-9(x-3)^{2} & =-9({x}^{2}-6x+9) \\  & =-9{x}^{2}+54x-81.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-9{x}^{2}+54x-81.$
